corpus.work: Bhāgavatapurāṇa; electronic text contributed by Ulrich Stiehl, GRETIL, SUB Göttingen

search_scope: All unaccented occurrences of niśam/niśām immediately followed by y or ay in the TEI body, including longer tokens and joined next words. This excludes other suffixes, other preverbs without ni, and other works.
locators: Use the recorded XML line (one-based), Unicode character offset (zero-based in that line), and next original printed verse-end label, retaining any source asterisk. All five duplicated occurrences are exact repeats of the preceding XML line at the same verse label; both addresses remain in the table.

context_controls.context: niśāmaya + asmad-vacaḥ forms niśāmayāsmad-vaca in connected text.
Nārada is speaking; the addressee is invited to hear the secret.
Genitive singular niśāmayantyāḥ agrees with merudevyāḥ; the surface visarga is absent before voiced m. GRETIL 5.3.18 corresponds to 5.3.19 in the glossary edition.
Feminine genitive plural niśāmayantīnām agrees with prajānām. The citizens are listening as the sons are instructed.
The short-vowel absolutive is applied to chanting heard from the mouth of a dying man.
The object of the absolutive is what a son said; niśamya + etat gives niśamyaitat.
The observers find the waterpot empty. The short-vowel absolutive niśamya joins atha.
The cowherds open their eyes before perceiving themselves and the cows safe. This is short-vowel niśamya.
Long-vowel niśāmya applies to witnessing the display of Kṛṣṇa.
The command niśamyatām takes singular etat, while the two called by name are dual. Position and number are different from an active 2du.
Masculine nominative singular niśāmayan agrees with vipraḥ. The subject returns home upon hearing of Arjuna’s prowess.
Etaiḥ directs the addressee to recognize rajas by its signs; the imperative is niśāmaya.

other_senses: The other 100 grammatical tokens have an identified construction; their individual perception senses remain open here.

operations.absolutives: Identify the previous action on the shared subject, retaining the preverb and the lyap construction under 3.4.21 and 7.1.37. Vowel sandhi against the next word is recorded separately.
operations.participles: niśāmayat-/niśāmayantī- are nominal forms. Assign agreement from their own head, including the singular genitive before voiced m.
operations.two_commands: niśāmaya is an active 2sg imperative. At 10.36.22 niśamyatām has the passive yak and a 3sg ending; the singular demonstrative, not the dual vocative pair, supplies its agreement.
operations.projection: Retain the source locator, root-vowel length, suffix class, agreement, co-text and any following-word boundary. The two short-vowel visual absolutives and the long-vowel hearing forms show that a vowel-to-sense lookup cannot recover the source interpretation.
